name: AIJ UWE benchmark — cleaned release, Cases A-E

licence.note: The measurement data belongs to its collectors and distributors, named per case. Cite the benchmark paper and each case's requested citation.

cite.benchmark: Kikumoto, H., Okaze, T., Yoshie, R. et al. (2026). Comprehensive Experimental Database for Validating CFD Simulations in Urban Wind Environment: Benchmark Cases Curated by the Architectural Institute of Japan. Japan Architectural Review 9(1), e70083. https://doi.org/10.1002/2475-8876.70083

built_by: clean/build.py (deterministic; re-run to regenerate; checks.json carries the validity checks, build.log every transform)

case_id.meaning: AIJ UWE case letter, A to M

config.meaning: configuration within the case: 'default' (A, B, D); Case C centre building '0D' | '1D' | '2D'; Case E 'bc' (before construction) | 'ac' (after construction)

instrument.meaning: 'split_fibre' = hot-wire split-fibre probe, vector components; 'thermistor' = omnidirectional scalar speed

point_id.meaning: the tunnel's own measurement point number (No.); shared across configurations and directions of a case

wind_direction_deg.meaning: the case's wind direction label. A-D: the AIJ turntable angle WD (0 = +x). E: meteorological FROM-direction, clockwise from north (N = 0, E = 90). The flow vector per direction is in directions.csv

wind_direction.meaning: compass name of the FROM-direction (Case E only; '' elsewhere)

x.meaning: case frame (SCHEMA.md): +x = streamwise at WD = 0 for A-D, +x = east for E; model-scale metres for A-D, full-scale metres for E

V.meaning: mean velocity component along +y (positive toward +y in EVERY case; Case B's published sign is flipped, see manifest transform)

uu.meaning: variance of the x-component fluctuation <u'u'> (Case A publishes rms; squared here)

k.meaning: turbulent kinetic energy as published (= (uu+vv+ww)/2 wherever all three variances exist; checked)

Vs.meaning: mean omnidirectional SCALAR wind speed from a thermistor anemometer. NOT |mean velocity vector| (Case D's split-fibre |U| column is dropped, see log)

velocity_ratio.meaning: Case E: Vs / U_ref with U_ref = the approach-flow speed at z = 15.9 m (full scale); see manifest cases.E.normalisation

campaign.meaning: 'wind_tunnel' (model scale) or 'field' (a full-scale observation: Cases F, G, M)

run.meaning: replicate label within a campaign where the dataset publishes individual runs (Case M); empty elsewhere

C.meaning: mean tracer-gas concentration as published (volume fraction x 1e6 of the released gas diluted in air)

concentration_ratio.meaning: C / c0, c0 = q / (U_ref L_ref^2) as the benchmark defines it for the case (manifest cases.<id>.normalisation)

T.meaning: mean air temperature as published (Cases J, L)

velocity_ratio_sd.meaning: standard deviation of velocity_ratio over the observations behind a field value (Case F)

k_ratio.meaning: k / U_ref^2 where the dataset publishes only normalised values (Case G; U_ref = U at the tree height)

E.status_note: Case E: points and inflow are released at full precision from the official workbook and pass every check; what stays provisional is the GEOMETRY of the before-construction state (an Eddy3D reconstruction with no published source) and the open questions in QUESTIONS.md (Q3).

inflow.epsilon_note: the sheet defines epsilon(z) = Pk(z) = Cmu^0.5 k(z) dU/dz with Cmu = 0.09

known_issues.csv_unit_of_T: RS_caseJ.csv, AF_caseJ.csv and BD-ST_caseJ.csv give temperature in KELVIN; the table carries degC (T) and K (T_rms, a difference)
known_issues.duplicate_row: RS_caseJ.csv No. 1 and No. 153 are the same row (-0.16, 0, 0.004)
known_issues.published_resolution: the CSV is the workbook's ratios rounded to 1e-3 (U, V, W) or 1e-4: heat fluxes sit on a 0.0049 K m/s grid, k on 0.00021 m2/s2; the table uses the workbook values
known_issues.fill_series_uncertainty: workbook sheet xy-plane2, column AH (Ue of the w'theta' flux): 193 cells are 0.0037 + a running integer, not an uncertainty
known_issues.readme_reynolds_number: readme 43,000, data paper 1.6e4 (U_H H / nu); 43,000 is Case H's
known_issues.no_shear_stresses_at_points: uv, uw, vw are published only for the approach flow
known_issues.c0_includes_gas_fraction: c0 = 12.283 ppm contains the 5 % ethylene fraction of the released gas; q / (U_H H^2) alone is 245.7 ppm; the data paper states no c0 for J (QUESTIONS.md QJ2)
known_issues.variance_vs_sigma: the workbook's <u'2>, <v'2>, <w'2> differ from the squares of its sigma columns by up to 3 % in single rows; the table uses the variances, which reproduce k (QUESTIONS.md QJ4)
known_issues.expanded_uncertainty: the workbook lists an expanded uncertainty beside every quantity (summary in extra_measurements.expanded_uncertainty); the mean concentration does not exceed its own (about 1 ppm) at 197 of 465 rows
known_issues.inflow_stations: the empty-tunnel profile at x/H = 0 and +2.5 differs from the published one at x/H = -2.5 near the ground (cases/J/approach_flow_full.csv; QUESTIONS.md QJ5)
known_issues.readme_T_b: the readme's T_b = 285.32 K is the approach-flow air temperature at z = H, not the building (121 measured surface points: 22.0 .. 28.9 degC, cases/J/surface_temperature.csv)

expanded_uncertainty.where: LF_caseJ.xlsx, sheets xz-plane(Unstable state), xy-plane(Unstable state), xy-plane2(Unstable state) and Unstable Inflow: every measured quantity has a 'Measurement' column and an 'Expanded Uncertainty: Ue' column beside it, in the workbook's non-dimensional units; the table has no column for it. per_quantity is in physical units over the 465 workbook rows of the three measurement sheets (columns are the table's names, su/sv/sw = the rms columns)
expanded_uncertainty.coverage_factor: not stated in the workbook (ISO/IEC Guide 98-3 per the data paper)

approach_flow_full.source: LF_caseJ.xlsx 'Unstable Inflow' (three stations x = -0.4, 0, +0.4 m, no building)
